strings.name: Anwar Ibrahim
strings.role: Prime Minister of Malaysia · Reform politician
strings.summary: Anwar moved from student and Islamic youth activism into government, serving as finance minister and deputy premier. His dismissal in 1998 made him a symbol of reform. He denied the legitimacy of charges that repeatedly imprisoned him; the IPU questioned trial fairness. Fully pardoned in 2018, he became coalition prime minister after the hung parliament of 2022, focusing on living costs, economic reform and coalition coordination.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Long involved in Malaysia’s reform movement before entering government leadership, his coalition politics and economic governance have regional influence.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Cherok Tok Kun, Bukit Mertajam, Penang.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Opposition to premiership
strings.highlights.h1.text: A longtime reform activist, became Malaysia’s tenth prime minister in a coalition government in 2022.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Malay College Kuala Kangsar; higher education at the University of Malaya from 1968.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Imprisonment and pardon
strings.highlights.h2.text: Repeatedly tried and imprisoned, received a full royal pardon in 2018; a pardon differs from acquittal.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Living-cost measures
strings.timeline.t1.text: Announced higher subsidised-fuel quotas and funding for schools and small traders.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Sworn in as premier
strings.timeline.t2.text: Became tenth prime minister after post-election coalition negotiations.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Full royal pardon
strings.timeline.t3.text: The king’s full pardon ended his imprisonment at that time.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Imprisoned again
strings.timeline.t4.text: The Federal Court upheld his sodomy conviction; the IPU questioned trial fairness.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Opposition leadership
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became opposition leader, continuing the reform agenda.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Dismissal and arrest
strings.timeline.t6.text: Dismissed as deputy premier and later arrested, turning to opposition politics.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Deputy prime minister
strings.timeline.t7.text: Advanced to deputy premier after several ministerial posts.
strings.timeline.t8.title: University studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Pursued higher education at Malaya and became active in student politics.
